newsitem.title: UK: UK gas deregulation means poor pay more - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: UK gas deregulation means poor pay more - watchdog.

text.p: Britain's gas consumer watchdog said poorer families could face higher gas bills than wealthier customers as competition is widened to cover a further 1.5 million households on Monday.
The Gas Consumers Council said on Sunday that customers with credit and bank accounts who pay by direct debit can expect to gain more than poorer customers using pre-payment meters.
"We would, of course, expect there to be a range of tariff prices...but some of these gaps seem socially unacceptable," said GCC Director Sue Slipman in a statement.
At present, British Gas customers on pre-payment meters -- often on low incomes or benefits -- pay 14 percent more than those who pay by direct debit, the GCC said.
"In opening up the domestic gas market to competition, Parliament intended that it should benefit all consumers regardless of their income level or payment method," said Slipman.
"The yardstick was that companies would take the price and customer service base line established by British Gas and improve upon it."

But in a survey published today, the GCC found that in the next stage of competition, pre-payment customers were set to be charged an average of 26 percent more than those paying by direct debit but using the same amount of gas.

After stripping out introductory offers, one supplier, Midlands Gas Ltd, was set to charge 38 percent more to customers on pre-payment meters, while Calortex, along with British Gas offered the best deal with a 14 percent gap in charges, the survey revealed.
"If this became a trend in future price offerings it would mean that the poorer consumers end up with no choice of supplier," the GCC said in the statement.
"We do not believe it is in the public interest for the poorest to pay the most, and want to support the industry to find more cost effective ways of supplying consumers on pre-payment meters."
Fifteen companies have been licensed to supply gas in Phase Two of competition in which 1.5 million households will join the 500,000 already allowed to pick their gas supplier.
Residents in Avon and Dorset will join those in the Phase One areas of Devon, Somerset and Cornwall on Monday. Kent and East and West Sussex will be added to the pilot area on March 7.
